nodes.name: Render driver
nodes.responsibility: Coordinates the current passes
nodes.description: Current paintArchitecture orchestrates relieveCongestion, route painting, label settlement, card painting and atlas creation. This sequence groups those helper calls by responsibility; it is not a new runtime module.

nodes.name: Card text
nodes.responsibility: Fits words into allocated space
nodes.description: Current fittedSize measures title widths and reduces type size to its floor. SVG card painting then applies measured ellipsis to titles and single-line responsibilities. The existing font measurement engine remains authoritative.

nodes.name: Grid placement
nodes.responsibility: Assigns fixed seats and rows
nodes.description: Current layoutArchitecture uses region bands, global rows and paired seats. cardHeight is46 or58 units depending on responsibility presence. Card text does not grow the card; title size fits the available width.

nodes.name: Route planning
nodes.responsibility: Plans indexed corridors and ports
nodes.description: Current relieveCongestion counts planned channel traffic and expands gaps before final routeEdges. Routes use grid bands/corridors. Label settlement happens later in paintEdges, before marks are emitted.

nodes.name: SVG marks
nodes.responsibility: Fits and paints the final marks
nodes.description: Current paintCard truncates title and responsibility using real font metrics. The architecture painter also settles edge-label boxes, emits marks and derives atlas bounds from actual geometry.

beats.heading: Fixed space comes first
beats.body: The grid chooses card space. Text fitting reduces the title size, and painting may still ellipsize it. Responsibilities remain one line. This is the behavior the proposal replaces.

beats.heading: Routing and labels follow placement
beats.body: Congestion relief can expand grid gaps and repeat placement. Final routes are produced after that; label boxes are settled in the architecture paint orchestration. The existing renderer already returns SVG and matching atlas bounds.

beats.heading: Words first, then space
beats.body: Nothing is placed before it is measured. The size a name needs is a fact the layout is handed, in the face the SVG will paint, so no later pass has to make room it did not reserve.

beats.heading: Pretext breaks lines; the renderer owns card policy
beats.body: Pretext is given a prepared string and a width and hands back lines. Padding, icon space, baselines and the bounds a card may take are the renderer's, not the library's.

beats.heading: One owner places and routes
beats.body: Graphviz places the cards and frames, libavoid routes every relationship around them, and the labels settle on those routes, all under one owner. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate, which is why there is no second geometry to keep in step.

beats.heading: Every board reads down; a fold must earn its place
beats.body: Every variant is laid out fresh and reads top to bottom. A settled drawing folds into more columns only when that fits the reference pane materially better, and fewer columns win a tie. Nobody authors the reading.

beats.heading: The painter decides no geometry
beats.body: By the time the painter runs, every box, port, route and label box is settled. It paints what it is given, so the picture a reader points at and the atlas the inspector reads are the same geometry.

beats.heading: Words first, then space
beats.body: Nothing is placed before it is measured. The size a name needs is a fact the layout is handed, in the face the SVG will paint, so no later pass has to make room it did not reserve.

beats.heading: Pretext breaks lines; the renderer owns card policy
beats.body: Pretext is given a prepared string and a width and hands back lines. Padding, icon space, baselines and the bounds a card may take are the renderer's, not the library's.

beats.heading: One engine places and routes
beats.body: Track or Blocks lays the board out, one block at a time from the innermost. Graphviz ranks a block's cards and its lines run on tracks between the ranks; libavoid routes the trunks between packed blocks. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate, which is why there is no second geometry to keep in step.

beats.heading: The drawing that reads best is kept
beats.body: A board is solved more than one way, and the answers are weighed as drawn: crossings, line length and how well it fits the reference pane, which is as wide as the shell gives a drawing and as tall as the tuned 1.4 page shape makes that width, not the shell's own pane (ADR 0043). A block of cards wraps a wide rank or folds tall ranks into columns only where that reads better. Nobody authors the reading, and every variant is laid out fresh.

beats.heading: The painter decides no geometry
beats.body: By the time the painter runs, every box, port, route and label box is settled. It paints what it is given, so the picture a reader points at and the atlas the inspector reads are the same geometry.

nodes.responsibility: Lays the board out as blocks, keeps the solve that reads best and makes its geometry the drawing
nodes.description: Join candidates run in parallel and retain the same comparison order. When a kept candidate changes the remaining choices, the renderer cancels obsolete queued candidates. Active solves finish normally.

nodes.name: Entry row
nodes.responsibility: Stands each container's hidden parts below its first entry points, so the parts its callers reach take its first row
nodes.description: Track only (ADR 0044). A first entry point is one no other part of the container leads to on the variant, as the compound graph marks it. Each other hidden part is held below it by an invisible edge that ranks and pulls nothing; an edge that would close a loop is left out, so a hidden part that calls an entry point stands above it.

nodes.name: Draw and measure
nodes.responsibility: Measures every card and label in the renderer core, then paints the settled drawing, and decides no geometry of its own

nodes.name: Engine and graph
nodes.responsibility: States the board as one graph of containment, sizes and relationship kinds, and lays it out through the engine a render names, inside a layout worker

nodes.name: Block layout
nodes.responsibility: Chooses between the solves of one board: asks for them side by side across the worker pool and keeps the one that reads best, as the core weighs them
nodes.description: Only block-engine.ts, solves.ts and joins-laid.ts are left here, on the main thread, for both engines. The renderer core lays out every solve, and what a choice weighs is the core's too: drawsBetter, readsBetterPacked, stacksOf, joiningOf and hasRegions (TASK-520.05, docs/agents/boundaries.md).

nodes.name: Orthogonal router
nodes.responsibility: Routes orthogonal connectors around rectangles, nudged a lane apart
nodes.description: archboard-router, linked into the renderer core: an A* search over the grid of the obstacles' buffer edges that pays for each turn and crossing, then nudging that stands the routes on one line a lane apart in the order they part. Written from the published papers it cites, not from libavoid. A connector it cannot route comes back empty, and nothing throws.

nodes.name: Board layout
nodes.responsibility: Lays out every Track and Blocks solve in the renderer core: ranks cards with the host's Graphviz, routes lines on tracks, packs blocks and routes their trunks, and assembles the drawing
nodes.description: crates/archboard-layout, linked into the renderer core. Its interface is one function, lay_out_board(graph, &mut dyn Graphviz), which takes the measured graph as the JSON of an ELK node, its root options naming how the containers and group regions are drawn (blocks, inline or groups), and answers the root of the drawing; the pure choice functions draws_better, reads_better_packed, stacks_of, joining_of and has_regions, which weigh what solves told where the renderer chooses between them; and one trait, Graphviz, which the binding satisfies with the host's viz-js. The wasm binding exports them as layOutBoard, drawsBetter, readsBetterPacked, stacksOf, joiningOf and hasRegions (crates/archboard-renderer-wasm/src/layout.rs). It answers what the TypeScript stage answered, to the bit (ADR 0057, docs/design/layout-rules.md).

nodes.name: Text shaping
nodes.responsibility: Shapes words into glyphs in the faces the core carries, breaks a paragraph to a width, and draws each glyph's outline
nodes.description: crates/archboard-text: shape (harfrust), width, outline (Skrifa, unhinted) and Paragraph (lines, line_count, natural_width, balanced_width, fewer_lines_at). A paragraph breaks where UAX #14 allows, after any space and never after a slash, its spaces hang, and an overlong word breaks between graphemes. Onest and DM Mono at 400 and 500 are built into the core from packages/renderer/assets/fonts, with Noto faces for the Greek, symbols and math they lack. A width is taken to a hundredth of a unit in single precision, as the canvas gave it before.

beats.heading: Words first, then space
beats.body: Nothing is placed before it is measured. The core shapes each name in the face the picture draws it in, and the size it needs is a fact the layout is handed, so no later pass has to make room it did not reserve.

beats.heading: The text module breaks lines; the renderer owns card policy
beats.body: The core's text module is given words, a face, a size and a width and hands back lines. Padding, icon space, baselines and the bounds a card may take are the measuring module's, not the text module's.

beats.heading: One engine places and routes
beats.body: Track or Blocks lays the board out, one block at a time from the innermost, and the renderer core lays out every solve of either. Graphviz ranks a block's cards and its lines run on tracks between the ranks; the orthogonal router of the core routes the trunks between packed blocks. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate, which is why there is no second geometry to keep in step.

beats.heading: The drawing that reads best is kept
beats.body: A board is solved more than one way, and the answers are weighed as drawn: crossings, line length and how well it fits the reference pane, which is as wide as the shell gives a drawing and as tall as the tuned 1.4 page shape makes that width, not the shell's own pane (ADR 0043). A block of cards wraps a wide rank or folds tall ranks into columns only where that reads better. The core weighs the drawings, and the renderer keeps the one it says reads better. Nobody authors the reading, and every variant is laid out fresh.

beats.heading: The painter decides no geometry
beats.body: By the time the painter runs, every box, port, route and label box is settled. It paints what it is given, so the picture a reader points at and the atlas the inspector reads are the same geometry.
